messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — customer on private (VPC) is seeing 502/503s and TLS handshake failures when Redwood Private components try to call our control plane. They suspect their k8s CNI / networkpolicy is blocking egress. Logs attached from their side.

marie_sre: Can you paste the exact error they're seeing from the pod logs? Also which CNI (calico/cilium/flannel) and any active NetworkPolicy in the redwood namespace?

alex_support: From customer: `time="2024-06-05T14:02:17Z" level=error msg="upstream request failed: Post \"https://control.redwood-private.prod:8443/v1/ping\": EOF"` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in some cases. They run Cilium and have a default-deny egress policy in their tenant namespaces.

ben_oncall: Quick checklist: DNS, egress rules to control plane IPs/ports (8443/443), and TLS interception. Also confirm kube-dns/CoreDNS can reach upstream (53). The common pattern: NetworkPolicy denies egress to the control plane IPs or to kube-system DNS.

marie_sre: Ask them to run a debug pod and reproduce:
``` 
kubectl run --rm -it debug --image=radial/busyboxplus:curl -- /bin/sh
# inside pod
nslookup control.redwood-private.prod 8.8.8.8
curl -v --resolve control.redwood-private.prod:8443:10.2.3.7 https://control.redwood-private.prod:8443/v1/ping
# or curl by IP to avoid DNS issues
curl -v https://10.2.3.7:8443/v1/ping
```
If the curl hangs or times out -> egress blocked. If curl connects but TLS fails -> CA/inspection issue.

alex_support: Customer ran a debug pod. Results: `curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.2.3.7 port 8443: Connection timed out`. nslookup to 8.8.8.8 succeeds, but their pods use a custom DNS policy — we asked them to test DNS resolution from inside the pod to the control host and to do tcpdump.

tariq_eng_priv: Also ask for evidence from their CNI: Cilium logs will show `DENIED` traces for policy rejects. For calico you'd see `DROP` in flow logs or iptables rules. Request `kubectl get networkpolicy -A -o yaml` and `cilium monitor` output if Cilium.

ops_bot: automated-note: escalations with networkpolicy causing private connectivity issues often resolved by adding namespace-level egress allowlist for control plane ranges and DNS. See runbook ID RP-PRV-008. :page_facing_up:

marie_sre: If they have default-deny egress, they need to add an explicit egress rule for the redwood namespace. Example NetworkPolicy (Cilium/Calico compatible):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-egress
  namespace: redwood-private
spec:
  podSelector: {} # all pods in namespace
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.2.3.0/24 # control plane IPs (replace with your range)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

ben_oncall: Important: if they're doing TLS inspection (corporate firewall/strand in path) that can swap the cert and cause `x509` errors. Two mitigations: 1) allow passthrough to control plane hosts (no TLS MITM), or 2) add the TLS MITM CA into the pod image/trust store (not ideal).

alex_support: Customer provided `kubectl get networkpolicy -n redwood-private` output — they have a DenyAll egress policy. We sent the sample policy above. They also said their firewall egress allowlist is IP-based and currently only allows 443 to external SaaS, not 8443.

tariq_eng_priv: For immediate triage ask them to: 1) temporarily remove/relax the egress deny in that namespace OR 2) add rules to allow egress to our control plane IPs on 8443 and to DNS servers (53 UDP/TCP). Also ensure hostNetwork pods (like egress gateways) are allowed to forward traffic.

marie_sre: Repro steps for us if they claim it's not networkpolicy: 1) we spin a debug pod in their cluster via their support access; 2) run `tcpdump -n -i any host 10.2.3.7 and port 8443` while issuing curl; 3) check CNI monitor logs for DENIED/REJECT. If no packets leave -> networkpolicy/firewall. If SYNs reach but no SYN/ACK -> firewall/NACL.

alex_support: Customer relaxed the policy for the namespace and curl to 10.2.3.7 succeeded immediately. They now get a 200 from /v1/ping. They will update their infra to permanently allow redwood control plane ranges and add 8443 to their egress allowlist.

ben_oncall: Follow-ups: ask them to confirm whether they want us to provide the canonical list of control plane IPs/CIDRs and FQDNs (we can export current set). Also ask if they'd prefer hostname-based egress rules (DNS reliance) vs IP-based allowlist.

marie_sre: I'll draft a small KB for the customer capturing: required egress ports (8443, 443, 80 for redirects, 53 DNS), recommended CIDRs, and troubleshooting commands (kubectl run debug, tcpdump, cilium monitor, curl examples). Will attach to the ticket.

alex_support: Great — customer confirmed fix strategy and requested the control-plane IP list. I'll provide it and close after they apply rules. :white_check_mark:
